title: Provisional Psychologist Salary: Hourly to Annual Conversion Under the Health Professionals Award
description: Convert your provisional psychologist salary from hourly to annual using Fair Work award rates. Includes tax, super, fortnightly pay, and casual loading.
salarySummary: A provisional psychologist at Level 1 under the Health Professionals and Support Services Award earns a minimum hourly rate of $32.44 (first year, AQF Level 5) to $40.56 (seventh year+), equating to an annual salary between $64,102 and $80,146 based on 38 hours per week.

faqs.q: What is the minimum hourly rate for a provisional psychologist in Australia?
faqs.a: Under the Health Professionals and Support Services Award 2020, a provisional psychologist classified as a Health Professional employee Level 1 with an AQF Level 5 qualification earns a minimum hourly rate of $32.44 in their first year, rising to $40.56 after seven years. These rates are set by the Fair Work Ombudsman and apply from the first full pay period on or after 1 July 2026.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from my hourly rate as a provisional psychologist?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by your weekly hours, then by 52. For a full-time provisional psychologist working 38 hours per week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. For example, $32.44 per hour gives an annual gross salary of $64,102. If you work part-time, use your actual weekly hours. This calculation assumes no unpaid leave, overtime, or penalty rates.

faqs.q: Does the provisional psychologist salary include superannuation and casual loading?
faqs.a: No. The award rates are base rates before super. Your employer must pay superannuation guarantee of 12% on top of your ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Casual employees receive a 25% loading on the base rate instead of paid leave. For a casual provisional psychologist, the hourly rate becomes $40.55 (first year) including loading.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Provisional Psychologist Salary

If you are a provisional psychologist in Australia, your pay is governed by the Health Professionals and Support Services Award 2020. This award sets minimum hourly rates for different classifications and experience levels. To plan your finances, you need to convert your hourly rate to an annual salary, understand tax and super, and know how casual or part-time work affects your pay. This guide uses the keyword **provisional psychologist salary** to help you navigate the numbers.

### Hourly to Annual Conversion Formula

The standard formula for converting an hourly rate to an annual salary is:

**Annual gross salary = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a full-time employee, the Fair Work Ombudsman defines ordinary hours as 38 per week. So the formula becomes:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52 = hourly rate × 1,976**

For example, a provisional psychologist earning the Level 1 first-year rate of $32.44 per hour would have an annual gross salary of $32.44 × 1,976 = $64,102. This assumes you work every week of the year with no unpaid leave. If you take four weeks of unpaid leave, use 48 weeks instead.

### Award Rates for Provisional Psychologists

According to the award, a Health Professional employee Level 1 is paid based on their AQF qualification and years of experience. For a provisional psychologist with a diploma or higher (AQF Level 5), the minimum hourly rates from 1 July 2026 are:

- 1st year: $32.44 per hour
- 2nd–3rd year: $34.44 per hour
- 4th–6th year: $37.53 per hour
- 7th year+: $40.56 per hour

These rates are higher than the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour. Always check your classification with your employer or the Fair Work Ombudsman.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your gross fortnightly pay, multiply your weekly pay by two. For a full-time provisional psychologist at $32.44 per hour:

- Weekly pay: $32.44 × 38 = $1,232.72
- Fortnightly pay: $1,232.72 × 2 = $2,465.44

Use the [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman to confirm your exact rates.

### Tax and Medicare Levy

Your annual gross salary is subject to Australian resident tax rates for 2026–27 and the Medicare levy (generally 2%). The tax brackets are:

- $0 – $18,200: Nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15%
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30%
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37%
- $190,001+: 45%

For a provisional psychologist earning $64,102 per year, the tax calculation is:

- Tax on first $18,200: $0
- Tax on next $26,800 (to $45,000): $4,020
- Tax on remaining $19,102 (to $64,102): $5,730.60
- Total tax: $9,750.60
- Medicare levy (2%): $1,282.04
- Total tax and Medicare: $11,032.64
- Annual take-home: $53,069.36

Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator for a precise estimate.

### Superannuation

Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid on top of your base salary. For a $64,102 salary, your employer contributes $7,692.24 to your super fund each year, up to the $270,830 maximum contribution base. This is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional benefit. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more details.

### Casual Loading

If you work as a casual provisional psychologist, you receive a 25% loading on the base rate instead of paid leave (annual leave, sick leave). For example, a first-year casual provisional psychologist earns $32.44 × 1.25 = $40.55 per hour. The annual equivalent is $40.55 × 1,976 = $80,126.80. However, casual employees do not accrue leave entitlements. Learn more about [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading).

### Comparing Offers: Base Rate vs Package

When comparing job offers, confirm whether the quoted hourly rate is the base rate (before super) or a package rate (including super). If a recruiter quotes $55 per hour including super, divide by 1.12 to get the base rate: $55 ÷ 1.12 = $49.11 per hour. The annual base salary is $49.11 × 1,976 = $97,041, with $11,645 going to super. Always clarify this before accepting an offer.

### Part-Time Work

Part-time provisional psychologists work fewer than 38 hours per week. Use your actual weekly hours in the formula. For example, 20 hours per week at $32.44 per hour gives an annual salary of $32.44 × 20 × 52 = $33,737.60. Part-time income may fall into lower tax brackets, and you may be eligible for the Low Income Tax Offset. Check the [reference tables](/data) for tax offsets.

### Key Takeaways

- The **provisional psychologist salary** under the Health Professionals Award ranges from $64,102 to $80,146 per year for full-time work.
- Always use 38 hours per week for full-time conversion unless your award specifies otherwise.
- Tax and Medicare reduce your take-home pay; super is additional.
- Casual loading adds 25% but removes leave entitlements.
- Use the [timesheet](/) to quickly convert your hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures.
